# ATP 3-21.8 Infantry Platoon and Squad (Excerpt)

## Squad Movement Formations

### Squad Column

Use the squad column formation when moving through restrictive terrain or under limited visibility.
This formation provides good control and rapid fire to the flanks.
Maintain dispersion between fire teams to reduce vulnerability to indirect fire.

### Squad Wedge

Use the squad wedge formation when enemy contact is possible but exact locations remain unknown.
The wedge places the squad leader behind the lead fire team for rapid visual control.

## Movement Techniques

### Traveling Overwatch

Use traveling overwatch when enemy contact is possible and speed remains necessary.
The trailing element follows about 50 meters behind the lead element and prepares to suppress.

### Bounding Overwatch

Use bounding overwatch when enemy contact is expected.
One fire team occupies a covered position to observe and suppress while the second team moves forward.

## Battle Drills

### React to Near Ambush

Soldiers inside the kill zone immediately return fire, throw smoke, and assault through the ambush.
Soldiers outside the kill zone establish base of fire support and suppress enemy positions.
